questions.question: Who is the author of the book The Buddha and His Dhamma?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Buddha and His Dhamma was authored by **B R Ambedkar__.**
 
• B R Ambedkar or Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was a famous Indian social reformer.
 
• He also inspired the Dalit Movement in India.
 
• Buddha and His Dhamma were one of his last works published in 1957 after his death which took place on 6 December 1956.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last Nawab of Awadh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wajid Ali Shah**__.

__
 
• Wajid Ali Shah was the eleventh and last King of Awadh.
 
• Lord Dalhousie, Governor General of British India, had deposed him under the pretext of misgovernance in February 1856.

• Begum Hazrat Mahal, also known as the Begum of Awadh, was the second wife of Nawab of Awadh Wajid Ali Shah.​

• Wajid Ali Shah was the eleventh and last King of Awadh.

questions.question: Which state of India was ruled by the Ahom Dynasty?
questions.solution:
• The Ahom dynasty ruled over present-day **Assam.**
 
• The dynasty ruled over Assam for almost 6 centuries from 1228 to 1826.
 
• The founder of the Ahom dynasty was Sukhapaa who came from Mong Mao, Mong Mao was a small medieval state located on present-day Myanmar-China border.
 
• The rule of the dynasty ended in the Burmese invasion of Assam in 1826.

questions.question: Byopa is a traditional headgear of tribes belonging to ______.
questions.solution:
• The Byopa is traditionally worn by **tribals of Arunachal Pradesh**
 
• It is mainly worn by people of the Nyishi tribe 
 
• The cap is mainly made of cane and is a warriors headgear to protect the head in war

questions.question: Wind turbines convert ________ energy into mechanical power.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Wind turbines convert **kinetic energy**__ into mechanical power.
 
• The kinetic energy is basically the energy of the moving wind.
 
• This energy is imparted to the blades of the turbine.
 
• The blades in turn, rotate a shaft which is connected to a generator that generates electricity.

questions.question: Which theory is used to make long-run predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system?
questions.solution:
• **The Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) Theory** can make long term predictions about exchange rates in a flexible exchange rate system.
 
• Basically PPP compares the economic productivity and standards of living of countries to predict exchange rates between different currencies.
 
• A simple formula for PPP is S = (P₁ / P₂) where 
 
 
• S is the exchange rate between two currencies 1 and 2
 
• P₁ is price of good X in country 1
 
• P₂ is price of good X in country 2 
 
 
 
• For an accurate prediction a range of goods should be compared with the PPP theory.

questions.question: Which of the following is the national sport of Bangladesh?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Kabaddi__ **is the national sport of Bangladesh.
 
• Despite that, cricket and football are much more popular in the country.
 
• Kabaddi is also known as Ha-Du-Du in the country.
 
• It is said that Kabaddi was decided as the national sport by the leaders of the country to break away from the colonial roots as both cricket and football are very famous British sports.

questions.question: What was the theme of World AIDS Day 2018?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The theme of World AIDS Day 2018 was '**Know Your Status**__'.
 
• The theme was set to bring awareness and urge people to check for the disease.
 
• AIDS day is celebrated annually on 1st December.
 
• 2018 marked the 30th anniversary of World AIDS day.

questions.question: Name the comprehensive pension management system developed by the Department of Telecom in December 2018.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The pension management system developed by Department of Telecom is known as **SAMPANN__.**
 
• SAMPANN stands for System for Accounting and Management of Pension.
 
• It is created by the Department of Telecom to allow senior citizens easier access to. their pensions.
 
• The system was announced in public by Prime Minister Modi on 29th December 2018 in Varanasi.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Saragarhi fought?
questions.solution:
• The famous Battle of Saragarhi was fought on **12 September of 1897.**
 
• The battle took place in Tirah which is in present-day Pakistan.
 
• It was fought between The British Indian Empire and Afghan tribesmen of the area.
 
• Only 21 Sikh soldiers fought for the British against about 10,000 tribesmen.
 
• The Sikh soldiers lost but fought till their deaths as a last stand.

questions.question: In which part of the body is blood produced?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Most constituents of blood are produced in the **bone marrow__** of human beings.
 
• Bone marrow is a type of spongy tissue that is present inside some bones of the body such as that of the hip.
 
• The red blood cells are made from stem cells in the bone marrow.
 
• The bone marrow produces about half a liter worth of red blood cells every week.
 
• It also produces 60-70% of the white blood cells.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest container port of India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Jawaharlal Nehru Port__ **is the largest container port in India.
 
• It is located in Navi Mumbai.
 
• The port alone handles about 40% of the countries ocean cargo.
 
• The port serves as the major cargo hub for Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

questions.question: Chepu is a unique cultural symbol of ______.
questions.solution:
• Chepu is a **prominent Nepali cultural symbol.**
 
• It is a decorative deity that is also known as the guardian of the house.
 
• It is believed in Nepali culture that it wards off evil spirits.
 
• Chepu is also known as Kirtikmukha or 'face of glory'.

questions.question: Who among the following is/was the longest serving governor of an Indian state?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **M M Jacob__ **has served the longest number of days as governor of an Indian state.
 
• He was the governor of Meghalaya.
 
• He served for a total of 11 years 293 days from 1995 to 2007.
 
• Next in line is Padmaja Naidu who served in West Bengal for 10 years 209 days from 1956 to 1967.
 
• Followed by N N Vohra who served in Jammu and Kashmir for 10 years and 59 days from 2008 to 2018.

questions.question: As of April 2019 who is longest serving chief minister of an Indian state?
questions.solution:

• **Pawan Chamling__ **holds the title of the longest-serving chief minister of an Indian state.

questions.question: How many sessions of the Lok Sabha are normally held in a year?
questions.solution:

 Budget Session
 February to May
 
 

 Monsoon Session

 Winter Session
 November to Mid December
 
 

 
• During the sessions, the timings of the Lok Sabha are from 11 AM to 1 PM and 2 PM to 6 PM.

questions.question: Which theory in economics proposes that countries export what they can most efficiently and plentifully produce?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Heckscher-Ohlin Model**__ proposes that countries export what they can produce very efficiently and in high quantities.
 
• It is also popularly known as the H-O Model or 2x2x2 model.
 
• It is used to examine the trade equilibrium between two countries.
 
• It takes into consideration that countries should ideally export materials and resources of which they have an excess, while proportionately importing those resources they need.

questions.question: In which medical condition is the eye's optic nerve damaged and the condition worsens over time?
questions.solution:
• **Glaucoma** is the medical term given when a person's optic nerve is damaged and worsens over time.
 
• Most common symptom of the condition is slow loss of vision.
 
• The condition is can not curable but treatment can reduce the loss of vision.

questions.question: In December 2018, Havelock Island was renamed as ________.
questions.solution:
• Havelock Island was renamed as **Swaraj Dweep** in 2018.
 
• The island is part of Ritchie's Archipelago in the Andaman Islands.
 
• The island is a famous tourist destination for its diving sites and scenic beaches.
 
• It is 90 minutes away from the capital of the Islands, Port Blair by ferry.

questions.question: Who was the first Russian prime minister to visit independent India?
questions.solution:
• **Nikolai Bulganin** was the first Russian Prime Minister to visit India after independence.
 
• The Prime Minister visited India in 1955.
 
• He was accompanied by Nikita Khruschev who was the Secretary of the Communist Party.
 
• They travelled to Punjab, Bombay, Bangalore, Madras and Calcutta and also some smaller towns.

questions.question: Which was the wettest place in India in 2018 as per the India Meteorological Department (IMD)?
questions.solution:
__
 
• According to the 2018 IMD survey, **Mahabaleshwar__ **is the wettest place in India.
 
• It received more rain (5,619 mm) than even Cherrapunji which was known to be the wettest place in the country for many years.
 
• This was because Cherrapunji received significantly less rainfall (4730 mm) compared to previous years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Mawsynram (Megalaya,India), the wettest place in the world, recorded an enormous 1003.6 mm of precipitation in 24 hours ending 8:30 am on June 17, 2022.
 
• This was the highest single-day rainfall recorded in June, while neighbouring Cherrapunji received 972 mm of rainfall, as per the India Meteorological Department (IMD)

questions.question: Identify the part of brain that controls the maintenance of posture, balance and equilibrium.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The cerebellum**__ is responsible for the maintenance of posture, balance and equilibrium.
 
• It is located behind the top part of the brain stem (where the spinal cord meets the brain).
 
• The cerebellum makes up about 10% of the brain's weight.
 
• Despite that, it contains about half of all the brains neurons (special cells that transmit information between sensory organs and brain).
 
• It is made up of two small halves.
